page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, 40 GB of local SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities but moderate multi-core performance due to the shared CPU allocation. Single-core stress-ng CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression place in the top 10% tier. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 397.31 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 46.59 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and memory scores are positioned in the bottom 25% tier.

This server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring high single-thread performance but low sustained multi-core utilization. The shared CPU allocation and low-capacity 40 GB SSD storage represent clear tradeoffs, making it less suitable for heavy database operations or large-scale LLM inference, where 7B model prompt processing drops to 14.06 tokens/sec. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, lightweight Redis caching, single-threaded data processing, and general-purpose development environments.
description: The UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is an x86_64 virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor, utilizing 2 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, 40 GB of local SSD storage, and one public IPv4 address. Benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between its top-tier single-core performance, such as single-threaded gzip compression and stress-ng single-core tests, and its weaker multi-threaded capabilities, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations landing in the bottom 25%. This resource profile presents a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core execution or high memory throughput. It is best suited for static web serving, lightweight Redis instances, and basic development tasks rather than resource-intensive database management or large language model inference.
